t:
Section 595 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1999 (Public Law 106–53; 113 Stat. 383; 128 Stat. 1316) is amended—
    (1) by redesignating subsection (h) as subsection (i); 
    (2) by inserting after subsection (g) the following:“(h) Eligibility.—“(1) In general.—Assistance under this section shall be made available to all eligible States and locales described in subsection (b) consistent with program priorities determined by the Secretary in accordance with criteria developed by the Secretary to establish the program priorities.“(2) Selection of projects.—In selecting projects for assistance under this section, the Secretary shall give priority to a project located in an eligible State or local entity for which the project sponsor is prepared to—“(A) execute a new or amended project cooperation agreement; and“(B) commence promptly after the date of enactment of the Water Resources Development Act of 2016.“(3) Rural projects.—The Secretary shall consider a project authorized under this section and an environmental infrastructure project authorized under section 219 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (Public Law 102–580; 106 Stat. 4835) for new starts on the same basis as any other similarly funded project.”; and 
    (3) in subsection (i) (as redesignated by paragraph (1)) by striking “which shall—” and all that follows through “remain” and inserting “to remain”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that references to States, local entities, project sponsors and a "project cooperation agreement" show outside-party involvement. But those parties are only recipients of assistance, and the Secretary alone sets the priorities and criteria and selects projects. The section requires no consultation, comment period, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue, and receiving assistance or signing a cooperation agreement is not participation in a federal decision.
fable.s: Assistance under this section shall be made available to all eligible States and locales described in subsection (b) consistent with program priorities determined by the Secretary in accordance with criteria developed by the Secretary

opus.w: The Secretary alone sets program priorities and selection criteria, and no outside party is consulted before those decisions are made. The mention of project sponsors executing 'a new or amended project cooperation agreement' is about entities getting assistance under a contract-like arrangement. That falls under the excluded category of benefit, grant, or contract applications. Nothing here requires rulemaking, a hearing, or a right to sue.
opus.s: consistent with program priorities determined by the Secretary in accordance with criteria developed by the Secretary to establish the program priorities.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions non-federal "project sponsor[s]" and "project cooperation agreement[s]" with eligible States and local entities. That could look like outside parties taking part in a federal decision. It fails against the definition. A sponsor signing a cooperation agreement or being ready to start construction is applying for, or contracting for, assistance, which the definition excludes. The Secretary sets the program priorities and criteria alone. Nothing requires consultation, a comment period, a hearing, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes how the Secretary determines program priorities and selects projects based on criteria developed by the Secretary. It does not require consultation with outside parties, public comment, or an advisory board with non-federal members. The process described is administrative selection based on internal criteria and project readiness, which does not constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: Assistance under this section shall be made available to all eligible States and locales described in subsection (b) consistent with program priorities determined by the Secretary in accordance with criteria developed by the Secretary to establish the program priorities.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "program priorities determined by the Secretary" implies a decision-making process that could involve public input, or that the mention of "eligible States and locales" implies consultation. However, the text explicitly states that the criteria are "developed by the Secretary," with no requirement for external input, comment periods, or advisory committees. The interaction described is primarily about eligibility and selection based on internal criteria and project readiness (executing agreements), which falls under administrative processing or grant application procedures rather than participatory decision-making. The definition excludes applications for grants and intra-governmental coordination. There is no mention of public hearings, comment periods, advisory boards with non-federal members, or required consultation with outside entities before the decision is made.
